name: faed_running_key_mod9_then_creator_checkerboard
idea: Treat FAED and DBBI as two streams over the same nine-symbol alphabet and run a classical running-key polyalphabetic (Vigenere, Beaufort and additive) of FAED against DBBI, its reverse and the prime-scaffold payload, mod 9. The resulting digit stream is then read with the creator's own keyed straddling checkerboard (alphabet FUBCDORA.LETHINGKYMVPS.JQZXW, escapes 1 and 4) from Stage 3.2.2, which is exactly the two-layer style the Architect block used. Both 0-8 and 1-9 digit renderings are decoded.
check: Any output that is readable English is an immediate hit; otherwise the strings are tried as passphrases for the SALPH blob and scanned for key shapes.
retro: Stage 3.2.1 used Beaufort with key THEMATRIXHASYOU; Stage 3.2.2 used this exact straddling checkerboard.

name: faed_autokey_mod9_primed_by_dbbi
idea: Run a classical autokey (both plaintext-autokey and ciphertext-autokey, in Vigenere and Beaufort forms) over the nine-symbol alphabet, decrypting FAED with DBBI or its payload as the primer. Autokey is the natural next cipher after a running key when the key is shorter than the message, and the Architect text explicitly promises a selection from many ciphers and intertwined passwords. Outputs are rendered as letters and decoded through the Stage 3.2.2 checkerboard.
check: Readable English in the output; otherwise the strings are tried as passphrases and key-shape scanned.
retro: Stage 3.2.1 Beaufort (same tableau family, fixed key); Stage 3.2.2 checkerboard for the second layer.

name: trifid_of_faed_on_dbbi_keyed_cube
idea: FAED's nine symbols are exactly two base-3 digits each, so the 570 letters are 1140 trits: a natural trifid ciphertext. Decrypt it as a trifid with the 3x3x3 cube filled by DBBI's symbols in order of first appearance (the same keyword rule that produced the Bifid square) followed by the remaining letters, over periods drawn from the puzzle's own counts (7, 13, 14, 23, 30, 31, 91). Both trit orders are tried.
check: English plaintext in an output line; strings are also tried as passphrases and key-shape scanned.
retro: Stage 3.2.1/D5 used the Polybius-square family (Bifid); trifid is the three-dimensional member never applied here.

name: playfair_decrypt_on_dbbi_keyed_square
idea: Playfair-decrypt FAED, DBBI and the Stage 3.2.2 answer letters on 5x5 squares keyed by DBBI (the D5 square and squares built from DBBI's and the payload's first-appearance order). Playfair is the digraph member of the same Polybius-square family the creator already used for the Bifid and checkerboard layers, and FAED's letters all lie inside the keyword block of that square, which is what a Playfair ciphertext restricted to the key part looks like.
check: Readable digraph plaintext; outputs also tried as passphrases and scanned for key shapes.
retro: D5's Bifid square and the Stage 3.2.2 checkerboard are the same square-keying idea.

name: dbbi_keyed_columnar_transposition_then_bifid
idea: Use DBBI's first w letters as a classical columnar-transposition key (alphabetical rank of the letters gives the column order) and both decrypt and encrypt FAED at widths taken from the puzzle's counts 7, 13, 14, 23, 24, 30, 31 and 91, then run the D5 Bifid on the rearranged text. A transposition before fractionation is the standard way a fractionated ciphertext resists a direct Bifid read, and the Architect explicitly speaks of intertwined layers.
check: English after the Bifid step; all outputs are tried as passphrases and key-shape scanned.
retro: D5's whole-block Bifid; Stage 0's spiral read is itself a route transposition.

name: dbbi_host_mask_as_grille_over_architect_text
idea: Tile the 91-position DBBI host mask (both the 31-position and 30-position variants) over the Architect text as a Cardan grille, at letter level and at word level, and read off the selected and the complementary streams. The dossier already shows that this exact walk applied to the Stage 3.2.2 answer splits it into two meaningful rails, so the creator plainly reuses the mask as a selector on running text.
check: A readable phrase in one of the rails; every rail is also tried as a passphrase.
retro: D3, where the same host positions were applied to the Stage 3.2.2 answer; Stage 0's spiral selection of coloured cells.

name: faed_base9_scalars_under_dbbi_keyed_decimation
idea: Eighty-one base-9 digits are exactly the size of a secp256k1 scalar, and FAED is 570 symbols over nine values. Select 81 of them by a classical skip/decimation cipher whose step sequence is DBBI (or the payload) read as digits 1-9, and also by the tiled host mask, then read the selection as a base-9 private key under both digit bijections. DBBI itself was already tested as a base-9 scalar; FAED under a DBBI-keyed selection was not.
check: Direct check of each 64-hex string against the prize address and the halving address.
retro: None directly; it is the FAED counterpart of the tested DBBI base-9 scalar reading.

name: nihilist_decrypt_of_faed_keyed_by_dbbi_coordinates
idea: Read FAED as 285 Nihilist numbers (each letter pair giving a two-digit group over 1-9) and subtract, as a Nihilist additive, the square coordinates of the DBBI letters on the D5 square; a borrowless per-digit subtraction mod 5 variant is included so every group lands back on the square. Nihilist is the classical additive-over-Polybius cipher and is exactly what a square-using author reaches for after the checkerboard and Bifid.
check: English plaintext among the 285-letter outputs; all outputs are tried as passphrases.
retro: The Stage 3.2.2 checkerboard and the D5 Bifid square supply the same coordinate system.

name: second_fractionation_of_the_bifid_tail_as_digraphs
idea: The Bifid output after BTCSEED is not random: its second letters cluster hard on B, C, D and E while its first letters vary, which is the signature of a digraphic coordinate code, not of noise. Take the tail two letters at a time and read each pair as a row/column pair on DBBI-keyed 5x5 squares (all four row/column pairings, two phases) to recover a single plaintext letter per digraph.
check: English plaintext, especially in the first line; outputs are also tried as passphrases.
retro: Stage 3.2.2's coordinate decode of a fractionated stream; the D5 Bifid square supplies the board.

name: gronsfeld_shifts_of_the_page_strings_keyed_by_dbbi
idea: Apply a Gronsfeld cipher (Vigenere with numeric key) to every decoded string on the final page, using the DBBI letters and the prime-scaffold payload read as digits 1-9 as the shift sequence, in both directions, plus the plain Caesar ladder and the reversal of each string. The page's own macro phrase says the answer is in front of your eyes but you are not seeing it, which is what a light shift over already visible words means.
check: Each short output is directly tried as a passphrase against the SALPH blob.
retro: Stage 1's passphrase was a plain visible lyric line; Stage 3.2.1 used a Vigenere-family shift over visible text.
